2.grammar: A broken plural noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, the case of the subject of a sentence or the thing being said to exist. Note there is no -n sound (no tanwīn) after the -u: that shows the word is not standing alone but is bound to a following noun, giving the sense 'garments OF …'.
2.root: ث-و-ب (th-w-b) — to return; hence a garment, and reward

3.meaning: Sundus — fine, thin, delicate silk, the soft inner weave prized as the most luxurious of cloths.
3.grammar: A noun. The -in ending (tanwīn with kasra) is the genitive case with indefiniteness: the -i vowel is what a word takes after a preposition or when it is possessed by a preceding noun ('… OF fine silk'), while the -n shows it is indefinite.
3.root: — (a borrowed word, of Persian origin, with no Arabic triliteral root)

4.meaning: Green — the colour of fresh growth and verdure, carrying in Arabic an association with lushness, freshness and life. This is the plural form, describing more than one green thing.
4.grammar: A plural adjective of colour (the plural of the pattern akhḍar / khaḍrāʾ). The -un ending (tanwīn with ḍamma) combines two signals: the -u vowel is the nominative case, used for the subject of a sentence or for a word describing a nominative noun, and the -n marks it as indefinite.
4.root: خ-ض-ر (kh-ḍ-r) — greenness, verdure, freshness

5.meaning: And brocade — thick, heavy silk shot through with gold thread, a stiff and glittering cloth, the counterpart to fine soft silk.
5.grammar: A noun preceded by the joining word 'and'. The -un ending (tanwīn with ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case of a subject, or of a noun joined by 'and' to another word already in the nominative.
5.root: — (a borrowed word, of Persian origin, with no Arabic triliteral root)

6.meaning: 'And they were adorned / given ornaments to wear' — to be decked with jewellery, bracelets and finery placed on one by another.

parts.en: adorned with ornaments (the u-vowel marks the passive)

6.grammar: Past-tense verb, Form II (doubled middle root letter, giving the sense of decking someone out), in the passive voice. The u-vowel in the stem is what makes it passive: they do not adorn themselves — the ornaments are put on them. The -ū ending is the subject marker 'they' for a group of males; the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

7.meaning: Bracelets, armlets — 'asāwir' is the plural of 'siwār', the band worn around the wrist or arm.
7.grammar: A plural noun of a special pattern (a 'diptote') that resists nunation; its -a ending serves as the accusative, typically marking it as the direct object (the thing received or acted upon). This plural shape ordinarily also stands in for the genitive without taking nunation.
7.root: س-و-ر (s-w-r) — bracelet, armlet; to enclose

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: Silver — fiḍḍatin is the noun fiḍḍa (silver) in the indefinite genitive. A precious metal used for ornamentation and currency.
9.grammar: Fiḍḍatin has the tanwīn kasra (-in) marking the indefinite genitive. The genitive case follows a preposition (min 'of/from silver') or appears in an adjectival/descriptive construction.
9.root: ف-ض-ض (f-ḍ-ḍ) — silver; to scatter, break apart

10.meaning: 'And He gave them to drink' — to hand someone a drink, to serve and quench them. The root covers watering, irrigating and pouring out drink for another.

parts.en: he gave to drink, he watered

10.grammar: Past-tense verb with a single male subject, 'he'. The stem ends in a weak letter written as long -ā (alif maqṣūra), the regular shape of such verbs in the third-person masculine singular past. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them', a group of males; the verb also takes a second object naming what is given to drink.
10.root: س-ق-ي (s-q-y) — to give drink, to water, to irrigate

11.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Nurturer who owns, provides, and brings to maturity) joined to the pronoun 'their'.
11.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -u vowel before -hum is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as the subject/doer. The suffix -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine plural group.
11.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

12.meaning: A drink, a beverage — anything served and swallowed as drink.
12.grammar: A noun. The -an ending (tanwīn with fatḥa) shows it is indefinite ('a drink') and places it in the accusative case, the case of the direct object of a verb.

13.meaning: Pure — and more than merely clean: the intensive pattern means purifying, something so pure that it cleanses whatever it touches, leaving no taint or impurity behind.
13.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿūl pattern, which strengthens the quality and adds the sense of making others share it — not just 'clean' but 'cleansing'. The -an ending (tanwīn with fatḥa) marks it as indefinite and accusative, the case it takes when describing a noun that is itself accusative.
13.root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r) — purity, cleanness, freedom from defilement

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

3.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

3.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

4.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

5.meaning: "as a recompense / requital / repayment" — a noun denoting the return or payment given for a deed, whether reward or penalty.
5.grammar: A masculine noun. The final "-an" (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative ending; on a word like this it commonly functions adverbially, expressing the cause, purpose, or manner — i.e., "(done) as a recompense."
5.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to recompense, requite, repay, reward or punish

6.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

7.meaning: Your striving — effort, exertion, the running and working a person puts into a pursuit. The root pictures brisk movement toward a goal, so this is active endeavour rather than mere intention.
7.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action itself) with a possessive pronoun attached. The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described. The final -kum means 'your' for a plural group of people addressed directly.
7.root: س-ع-ي (s-ʿ-y) — to strive, to walk briskly, to exert oneself

8.meaning: Thanked, appreciated, met with gratitude — describing effort that is acknowledged and repaid rather than overlooked. The root joins thanking with rewarding, so what is 'thanked' is also recompensed generously.

parts.en: prefix forming a passive participle: 'something that has been …-ed'

8.grammar: A passive participle — the ma- prefix with the -ū- pattern names the one who receives the action, so 'thanked' rather than 'thanking'. The -an ending (tanwīn with fatḥa) marks it as indefinite and accusative, the case used for a predicate after certain verbs and particles that govern the accusative.
8.root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r) — thanks, gratitude, grateful acknowledgement and reward

1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

2.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
2.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We sent down', 'We revealed', 'We caused to descend' — the form (with doubled middle letter) suggests a sending-down done gradually or emphatically, fittingly used of revelation.
3.grammar: This is a past-tense verb in an intensive pattern (the doubled middle consonant of nazzala). The '-nā' suffix is the attached subject marker meaning 'we', so the whole word reads 'We sent down'.
3.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, to come/send down

4.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

5.meaning: The Qur'an — the recited Scripture; literally 'the Recitation' or 'the Reading'.
5.grammar: A definite noun (carrying 'al-', 'the') on the verbal-noun pattern fuʿlān, denoting the act/thing of reciting. The final '-a' marks the accusative case, which most often signals that the word is the direct object of a verb.
5.root: ق-ر-ء (q-r-ʾ) — reciting, reading aloud, gathering words together

6.meaning: A verbal noun meaning 'a sending down / a bringing down by degrees'. It names the very act of causing something to descend, and is used as an emphatic restatement of that act ('a true sending-down').
6.grammar: A verbal noun from the intensive pattern, naming the action of sending down gradually. The final -an is the indefinite accusative; here this case typically marks the noun as an emphasizing object that reinforces a related verb ('We sent it down — a true sending-down'). The 'n' sound (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: A command meaning 'so be patient' or 'so endure steadfastly.' It calls for patient perseverance: bearing hardship, restraining oneself, and holding firm without complaint. The opening 'fa-' connects it to what precedes, giving the sense 'and so…' or 'therefore…'
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'be patient!' The vowelless final consonant (sukun on the -r) is the standard ending of a direct order. The prefixed 'fa-' is a connective particle meaning 'so' or 'therefore,' linking the command to a preceding statement.

2.meaning: For the command / decree of God — the Prophet is commanded to be patient, awaiting and under the judgment of his Lord.
2.grammar: Prepositional phrase: li + genitive noun ḥukm. Li-ḥukmi rabbika = 'for the judgment of your Lord' — be patient awaiting God's decree. Ḥukm (حُكْم) means judgment, ruling, command, or decree.
2.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to rule; حُكْم = judgment, decree, command

3.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

4.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
4.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

5.meaning: You obey, you comply with and submit to (someone's command); from a verb meaning to yield obedience.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form IV) in the jussive/apocopate mood. The tu- prefix marks 'you' (masculine singular). The bare ending (-ʿ with no final vowel) is the jussive form, used after particles like 'if' or negation/command particles, signalling a conditioned or non-indicative sense.
5.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — obedience, willing compliance

6.meaning: 'From them / of them' — a preposition of origin, source or partitioning joined to the pronoun 'them'. Depending on context it marks where something comes out of, or picks out some members from within a larger group.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. Prepositions put whatever follows them in the genitive, and here the pronoun -hum ('them', a group of males) is that object. The pronoun form -hum is the one used after prepositions and verbs; it does not change for case the way nouns do.
6.root: — (a preposition and a pronoun, with no root)

7.meaning: A sinner — one who commits sin, who incurs guilt and blame by wrongdoing. As an active participle it names the doer: the person actually engaged in sinning.
7.grammar: An active participle — the pattern names the one performing the action, hence 'a person who sins'. The -an ending (tanwīn with fatḥa) marks it as indefinite ('a sinner', not 'the sinner') and puts it in the accusative case, the case of a direct object.
7.root: أ-ث-م (ʾ-th-m) — sin, guilt, blameworthy wrongdoing

8.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
8.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

9.meaning: Means 'utterly ungrateful / deeply thankless' — one who intensely denies and covers over the favors received. The form stresses extreme, ingrained ingratitude.
9.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun pattern ('much/extremely …'). The -an ending is accusative, the state for an object or descriptive complement. The pattern conveys habitual, abundant ingratitude — not a slip but a settled trait of denying blessings.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, deny, be ungrateful

1.meaning: And remember, and mention — the command to remember Allah constantly in the heart and to mention His name with the tongue; dhikr encompasses both inner remembrance and vocal glorification.
1.grammar: The wa- is a conjunctive particle ('and'). udh'kuri is the imperative second-person masculine singular of the Form I verb dhakara (to remember, to mention). The hamzat al-waṣl (ا) is a connecting vowel dropped in connected speech. The final -i is a short kasra helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a consonant cluster in the following word; it is not a case ending.
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to commemorate

2.meaning: Name — the word or designation by which someone or something is called; in worship, the invoking of a name (especially Allah's) over an act.
2.grammar: A noun ('ism,' 'name'). The final '-a' (fatḥa) is the accusative case, the form typically used when the word is the direct object of a verb — the thing being acted upon.
2.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; the source of 'ism' (name)

3.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

4.meaning: Morning, daybreak, the early part of the day — the time from dawn until mid-morning.

parts.en: accusative ending on feminine noun (with nunation)

4.grammar: A feminine noun (its feminine ending is the tied-tā', pronounced '-t-' before the case vowel). The '-an' accusative ending here typically marks a time expression ('in the morning'), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.
4.root: ب-ك-ر (b-k-r) — early morning, to be early

5.meaning: 'And (in the) late afternoon/evening' — aṣīl is the closing stretch of the day, between late afternoon and sunset; often paired with morning to mean 'constantly, at both ends of the day'.
5.grammar: wa- is 'and'. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative; with time-words this case typically works adverbially — 'in the evening / at eventide' — telling when something happens.
5.root: أ-ص-ل (ʾ-ṣ-l) — root, origin, foundation; aṣīl is the day settling to its close

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
1.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

2.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
2.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').

3.meaning: 'So prostrate' — a command to place the forehead on the ground in worship, the posture of utter lowliness and submission before Allah, introduced by a connector meaning 'so' or 'then'.

parts.en: so, then (linking what follows to what came before)
helping vowel that lets the command be pronounced

3.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male. Because the verb's own stem begins with a consonant cluster, Arabic adds a helping vowel at the front to make it pronounceable; that vowel is dropped when the word is joined to what precedes it. The final consonant carries no vowel (a sukūn), which is the standard shape of this kind of command.
3.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, to bow down low in worship

4.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
4.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

5.meaning: A command to one person: "and glorify Him" — that is, declare Him utterly free of every defect, partner, or unworthy attribute, praising Him in a way that removes any imperfection from Him. The Form II verb of s-b-ḥ carries the idea of continually pronouncing His transcendence, whether by tongue, prayer, or heart.

parts.en: declare (Him) free of all imperfection, glorify

5.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one male person — "you, glorify!" The stem is the intensive/causative Form II (the middle root letter is doubled), which turns the root into "to pronounce something free of fault" rather than a simple action. The stem ends in a vowelless final letter (sukūn), the normal way an imperative closes. The attached -hu is the object pronoun "Him", showing who is being glorified.
5.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to glide/swim freely; in Form II, to declare Allah free of all imperfection

6.meaning: 'By night / during the night / a night' — the noun for nighttime, the dark hours.
6.grammar: A noun in the accusative indefinite, marked by -an (tanwīn). This ending is commonly used adverbially to express the time or circumstance of an action ('by night', 'at night').

7.meaning: "Long" — extended in measure, whether in time (a lengthy stretch, a long while) or in physical extent. It describes something drawn out and prolonged rather than brief.
7.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which describes a settled, lasting quality. The final -an is two things at once: the -n (nunation) marks the word as indefinite — "a long …" rather than "the long …" — and the -a is the accusative case. Accusative typically marks a direct object, an adverbial expression of extent or duration ("for long", "at length"), or an adjective agreeing with an accusative noun it describes.
7.root: ط-و-ل (ṭ-w-l) — length, extension, duration

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'These' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things that are near ('these ones, these here').
2.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'these,' used for near things or people (of either gender). It is built on a fixed base, but its final vowel reflects case: the -i here is the genitive form (hāʾulāʾi), required because it falls in a genitive position governed by the preceding preposition. This contrasts with the nominative form hāʾulāʾu — so the -i is a genuine case marker, not merely a connecting vowel.

3.meaning: "They love / cherish / hold dear" — to feel deep affection or fondness for someone or something. Describes an ongoing or habitual loving by a group.
3.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb with the yu-…-ūna frame meaning "they" (a group of males). The -ūna ending marks the plain present tense for a plural "they" subject (not negated, commanded, or made conditional). The yu- prefix belongs to this verb's particular pattern of loving.
3.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection, to hold dear

4.meaning: The fleeting, hastening one — the present, immediate life that passes quickly. Used as a name for this transient worldly existence, in contrast to the lasting Hereafter.
4.grammar: A feminine active participle ('the hastening one') with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as a direct object of a verb.
4.root: ع-ج-ل (ʿ-j-l) — to hasten, hurry, be quick

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'they leave behind' or 'they leave remaining' — to let something stay or remain after departing. Conveys leaving a thing in place.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), joined by wa- ('and'). The ya- prefix together with the -na ending mark a 'they' subject and the indicative mood, used for an ongoing or general statement of fact. This verb is used only in the present/imperative; it means to let remain or leave behind.
5.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — to leave, to leave behind (used only in present/command)

6.meaning: Behind them / beyond them / ahead of them — the word for 'behind' joined to 'them'. It can point to what lies after or in front, depending on vantage, with the sense of something looming on the other side.
6.grammar: A noun of place, 'behind/beyond', used adverbially like a preposition. The -a vowel is the accusative ending, the form often used for adverbs of place and time (telling 'where' or 'when'). The attached -hum is 'them' (a group, masculine), the party the location is reckoned from.
6.root: و-ر-ي / و-ر-أ (w-r-y / w-r-ʾ) — what is behind or beyond

7.meaning: A day; a defined stretch of time. Often used for a momentous appointed day such as a day of judgement or reckoning.
7.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a day'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative case, which typically marks the object of a verb or a noun otherwise governed in the accusative.
7.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time-period

8.meaning: "Heavy" — weighty, burdensome, hard to bear. Beyond physical weight it carries the sense of something momentous and grave, demanding effort and seriousness from whoever must carry or face it.
8.grammar: An adjective of the faʿīl pattern, expressing an inherent, stable quality. The closing -an shows indefiniteness through the -n (nunation) — "a heavy …" — while the -a is the accusative case, the form used for a direct object or for an adjective agreeing with an accusative noun.

1.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
1.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

2.meaning: We created them — a Form I perfect verb with first-person plural subject and third-person masculine plural object suffix.
2.grammar: Khalaqnāhum is a Form I perfect verb. Khalaq- is the perfect stem from kh-l-q (to create). -Nā marks first-person plural subject 'we'. -Hum is the third-person masculine plural object suffix 'them'.
2.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, to bring into being

3.meaning: "And We made firm / We strengthened, tightened, bound securely." The verb conveys fastening something so that it holds together solidly, giving it firmness and cohesion.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb: the action is presented as complete and accomplished. The suffix -nā is the subject ending meaning "we" — when Allah speaks of Himself this way it is the plural of majesty, not of number. Because the last two root letters are identical, the doubling unfolds into two separate letters before a consonant-initial ending, giving shadad-nā rather than shadd-nā.
3.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — firmness, tightness, strength

4.meaning: "Their frame" — the way a body is knit and joined together: its build, physique, the binding of its limbs and joints into one sound structure. The word comes from the idea of binding, so it pictures a form held tightly together.

parts.en: frame, build, the knitting-together of the body

4.grammar: A noun carrying an attached possessive pronoun. The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon); had it been genitive the vowel would be -i, and the pronoun would then be pronounced -him. The suffix -hum means "their", referring to a group of males or a mixed group.
4.root: أ-س-ر (ʾ-s-r) — to bind or tie firmly (hence asīr, a captive)

5.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
5.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

6.meaning: We willed / We wished — to will, want, or so decide; the deliberate exercise of will toward something.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending '-nā' marks a first-person plural subject ('we') performing a completed act of willing in the past.
6.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to want

7.meaning: "We could replace / We would exchange one thing for another." The Form II verb means to put something in the place of something else — to substitute, swap out, exchange — not merely to modify slightly. The past-tense form is also the normal Arabic way of stating a potential or conditional act, so it can read as "We can change" as much as "We replaced".
7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the intensive Form II (the middle root letter is doubled), which sharpens the root into deliberate, thorough substitution. The ending -nā is the subject pronoun "we"; used of Allah it is the plural of majesty. Arabic uses the perfect not only for a completed act but also, after conditional words, for an act that is potential or guaranteed to occur — hence a "could / would / will surely" sense in English.
7.root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l) — exchange, substitution, putting one thing in place of another

8.meaning: "Their likes / their likenesses" — the plural of mithl, 'something similar': people or cases of the same kind, those comparable to them.
8.grammar: A broken (internal) plural noun — mithl 'a like' becomes amthāl 'likes' by reshaping the word, not by adding a plural suffix. The -a is the accusative case marking it as an object of a verb, and -hum is the attached pronoun 'their'.

9.meaning: "A replacing, a substitution" — the abstract action-noun naming the very act of exchanging one thing for another. It names the deed itself rather than describing anyone doing it.
9.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) on the tafʿīl pattern, which is the standard action-noun of Form II verbs. The -n of the ending marks it as indefinite; the -a is accusative. A verbal noun in the accusative placed after a verb from the same root is the classic "absolute object", used to emphasise or intensify — the English feel is "replacing them a complete replacement", i.e. thoroughly.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

3.meaning: A reminder / an admonition — something that causes one to remember, a warning that brings to mind what is easily forgotten: duties to Allah, the reality of the Hereafter, and the stakes of one's choices.
3.grammar: Verbal noun (maṣdar) of Form II following the tafʿilah (تَفْعِلَة) pattern — a distinct Form II maṣdar variant, different from the more common tafʿīl (تَفْعِيل) pattern (which would yield tadhkīr). Feminine, singular, indefinite, in the nominative case. The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks it as nominative-indefinite, functioning as a subject or predicate.
3.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembering, mentioning, reminding

4.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
4.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
5.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.
5.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, wish

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'he took (for himself), adopted, or acquired' — to take something and make it one's own; from a reflexive pattern implying taking to oneself.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form VIII verb, third-person masculine singular ('he took'). Form VIII often carries a reflexive sense (taking for oneself). The final -a is the standard perfect ending, marking a completed act. The initial alif is a connecting hamza, sounded only at the start of an utterance.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
7.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

8.meaning: His Lord; the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings each thing to its completion. Rabb conveys ownership, authority, and loving care all at once.
8.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -hi meaning 'his.' The -i on the stem is the genitive ending, the case typically used after a preposition or to link a noun to a preceding one ('… OF …'); the pronoun then shifts to -hi to harmonize with that -i vowel, giving 'of his Lord / his Lord's.'
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship and ownership

9.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
9.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: "You (all) will, wish, want." The verb refers to an act of the will — to choose and desire something so that it may come about. It is stronger than idle wishing: it is willing that leads to a thing being so.
2.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, read tashāʾūna. The ta- prefix marks the person being spoken to, and the -ū of the ending makes it plural masculine, so prefix and suffix together mean "you (people) do X". In writing, the damma on the hamza plus the following wāw spell a single long ū, not two separate vowels, so the stem is shāʾ- and the ending -ūna. The final -na is the mark of the indicative mood — the form used for a plain statement of fact; it drops away when the verb is negated with lam or governed by particles meaning "that / so that". The root is hollow (its middle letter is weak), so the stem shows a long ā.
2.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to want

3.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
3.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
3.root: — (particle)

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
4.root: — (particle; no root)

5.meaning: '(that) he wills / wishes' — to will, intend, or so desire that a thing comes about.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he wills'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that/so that/until,' giving the sense 'that he should will.'
5.root: ش-و-ء (sh-w-ʾ) — to will, wish, want

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
6.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

9.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

10.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
10.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

11.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
11.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: "He admits / causes to enter" — the causative of 'enter': not to go in oneself but to bring someone in, to grant entry, characteristically used of Allah admitting people into the Garden.
1.grammar: The yu- prefix means 'he' in the present/future tense; its u-vowel (yu- rather than ya-) is the signature of the causative pattern (Form IV): 'make someone enter' instead of 'enter'. The final -u is the plain indicative mood — a straightforward statement of what he does or will do.

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

3.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
3.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
3.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
4.root: — (particle)

5.meaning: His mercy — His compassion, tenderness, and loving-kindness that actively bestows good and relief. "Raḥmah" is mercy as an outpouring of care, here possessed by Him.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun with an attached possessive "His." The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun or preposition ("… of …"). The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows that -i vowel.
5.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

6.meaning: "And the wrongdoers" — those who commit ẓulm: putting something where it does not belong, violating a right, acting unjustly. The gravest form is wronging oneself by associating partners with Allah or transgressing His limits; it also covers oppressing others.

parts.en: one who wrongs, an unjust person

6.grammar: An active participle — the pattern meaning "the one who does X" — made definite by al- "the", and put into the sound masculine plural. The -īna ending is the plural form used when the word is the object of a verb, follows a preposition, or stands in a possessive link; the contrasting -ūna ending is used when such a plural is the doer of the action. The l of al- assimilates into the following letter, which is why it is pronounced aẓ-ẓ-.
6.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to put something out of its rightful place; wrongdoing, injustice, darkness

7.meaning: He has prepared / made ready — to set something up in advance, to ready or get it in order beforehand.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he prepared'). It belongs to the 'form IV' pattern (the a- prefix gives the sense of actively making something ready). With no added subject suffix, the bare form means 'he' did the action, completed in the past. The doubled middle letter (shadda) is part of this root.
7.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — to count, prepare, make ready

8.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
8.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

9.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
9.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

10.meaning: "Painful" — causing acute, deeply felt pain. Its pattern can also carry an active sense: something that inflicts hurt, an anguishing torment.
10.grammar: An adjective of the faʿīl pattern, describing a fixed and intense quality. The final -an combines two signals: the -n (nunation) marks the word as indefinite — "a painful …" — and the -a is the accusative case, used for a direct object or for a describing word that takes the case of the noun it describes.
